headline: A Leaked npm Source Map Turns Claude Code Open-Source
lede: On March 31, 2026, Anthropic accidentally published the unminified source code for **Claude Code** — its terminal-based AI coding assistant — inside an npm package's source map. Within twenty-four hours a developer had forked it into *OpenClaude*, a community build that swaps Anthropic's backend for any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint.
body:
The mechanism of the leak is mundane but consequential. *Source maps* are metadata files that map minified, production JavaScript back to the original human-readable source. They exist to help developers debug; publishing one to npm means anyone who downloads the package can reconstruct the original code. Anthropic had not open-sourced Claude Code, so the inclusion was almost certainly an oversight — but npm's content-delivery network cached it globally before it was noticed.

The resulting repo, *openclaude* by Gitlawb on GitHub, preserves Claude Code's interface and tooling while replacing the hard-wired Anthropic API calls with a configurable *OpenAI-compatible shim*. That shim is a thin translation layer: any model provider that speaks the OpenAI REST protocol — NVIDIA's hosted endpoints, DeepSeek, local Ollama instances, and dozens of others — can slot in without modifying the core code. The screenshot in the original post shows a session running against z-ai/glm5 through NVIDIA's inference API.

The project attracted 1.1k GitHub stars and nearly five hundred forks within hours of going public, a signal that demand for a model-agnostic version of Claude Code had been building quietly. Claude Code's value is largely in its *agentic loop* — the scaffolding that lets a language model plan, execute shell commands, read and edit files, and iterate — not in any particular model's weights. By separating that scaffolding from Anthropic's API, OpenClaude effectively turns the interface into open infrastructure.

The legal position is ambiguous. Accidental publication to a public registry does not constitute an open-source license grant; Anthropic's code almost certainly remains proprietary under copyright. Whether the company pursues takedowns is a separate question from whether the leak was real. Historically, projects in this posture tend to survive longest when they rewrite the copied sections rather than redistribute them verbatim. As of the snapshot, the repo had thirty-one commits and active pull requests, suggesting contributors are already moving fast.

concepts.definition: A source map is a file that links minified or compiled JavaScript back to the original developer-written source code. When a package published to npm includes these maps, anyone who installs the package can read the original, pre-obfuscation source. Accidentally shipping them is a known security anti-pattern for proprietary projects.

A de facto standard HTTP interface, originally defined by OpenAI, that many model providers have adopted. Software that targets this interface can switch between providers — Anthropic, DeepSeek, Ollama, NVIDIA-hosted models — by changing a base URL and an API key, without rewriting application logic.

The control structure inside tools like Claude Code that lets a language model take multi-step actions autonomously: read a file, run a test, interpret the output, edit code, and repeat. The model's reasoning is the 'brain'; the loop is the scaffolding that connects it to real tools in the environment.

Anthropic's command-line coding assistant, which runs in a developer's terminal and can plan, write, test, and commit code through an agentic loop. It was a paid, closed-source product before the source map incident.

repos.summary: OpenClaude is a community fork of the Claude Code source code, built from the snapshot that became publicly accessible via an npm source map on March 31, 2026. It replaces Anthropic's proprietary API layer with a configurable shim supporting OpenAI-compatible endpoints, enabling use with 200+ models including Ollama, DeepSeek, and NVIDIA-hosted inference. At time of the snapshot it had 1.1k stars, 493 forks, and active contribution from the community.

fact_check: The claim that the source became public 'via an npm source map exposure on March 31, 2026' is plausible and consistent with known npm packaging mistakes, but the research sources provided do not independently corroborate the exact date or confirm Anthropic's response. The figure of '200+ models' refers to the breadth of OpenAI-compatible providers, not models tested or verified by the project — actual compatibility will vary.
